supporting_observations.claim: At 13:47:04 UTC, FILE-ORC-01 had a connection to the proxy at 10.56.20.30:8080 with 640,000,235 bytes sent and 39,230 bytes received; this is the large outbound transfer described by the alert.

The inventory says the Keystone backup agent uploads several hundred MB, so the transfer's size is consistent with an approved backup; the available record does not identify it as that agent or as a Keystone upload.
The transfer record identifies the proxy endpoint, but does not provide the external destination or the originating process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The large-transfer record contains connection metadata but no destination hostname, URL, or process attribution, so it cannot establish where the bytes went or what generated them (T280-00298).
claims_not_established: Whether the transfer was generated by the approved Keystone backup agent and sent to keystone-backup.net.
Whether the transfer contained expected backup data or sensitive data being exfiltrated.
Whether the transfer was authorized or malicious.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve the matching proxy transaction or TLS inspection metadata, if available, to identify the destination and request details for the 13:47:04 UTC transfer.
Collect FILE-ORC-01 process and network telemetry around 13:47 UTC to attribute the connection to a process and user or service account.
Review Keystone agent logs and backup-job status, including upload size and timing, to confirm or rule out a matching backup.
unrelated_findings: At 13:21 UTC, FILE-ORC-01 made a proxy CONNECT to downloads.cloud.com using an Apache HttpClient Java user agent; this is separate from the alerted 13:47 transfer and the service is not listed as approved (T280-00045, T280-00047, T280-00048).
